name: Febuxostat
sections: White crystalline powder, practically insoluble in water.

The CARES trial (>6,000 gout patients with CV disease) found higher cardiovascular and all-cause death versus allopurinol, prompting a 2019 FDA boxed warning; the European FAST trial did not confirm excess risk. First approval/introduction: Discovered by Teijin (1998); EU 2008 (Ipsen/Menarini); US FDA 2009 (Takeda).

Selectively inhibits both oxidised and reduced forms of xanthine oxidase, reducing uric acid production. Receptor / target profile: Non-purine selective xanthine oxidase inhibitor that blocks the molybdenum-pterin active site of both oxidised and reduced enzyme forms.
Hepatic – UGT1A1/1A8/1A9 conjugation; oxidation via CYP1A2, 2C8, 2C9
Summary: Bioavailability ≥49%; Tmax 1–1.5 h. ~99% protein bound. Glucuronidated and oxidised. Half-life 5–8 h. Mixed hepatic/renal elimination.
Chronic hyperuricaemia in gout (with urate deposition, tophi or gouty arthritis) in patients intolerant of or inadequately responsive to allopurinol
Prevention of hyperuricaemia in tumour lysis syndrome (120 mg, specialist use)
Start 40 mg once daily; increase to 80 mg if serum urate >6 mg/dL after 2 weeks
Gout-flare prophylaxis (colchicine or NSAID) for at least 6 months
Do not start during an acute attack
No adjustment for mild–moderate renal impairment
Dose to be individualised by the treating physician according to clinical response and tolerability.
CrCl 15–30: max 40 mg/day (US label); no adjustment mild–moderate.
Mild–moderate: no adjustment (max 80 mg); severe: not studied.
Cardiovascular death – avoid in established major CV disease unless no alternative
Gout flares on initiation – give prophylaxis (colchicine or NSAID) for ≥6 months
With or without food; limit alcohol, purine-rich foods and sugary drinks.
Serum urate (target <6 mg/dL; <5 mg/dL with tophi); LFTs at baseline and periodically; CV symptoms; TSH if symptomatic.
CONFIRMS (Becker et al., 2010) – febuxostat 80 mg more effective than allopurinol 300 mg in urate lowering.
CARES (White et al., NEJM 2018) – higher CV and all-cause mortality versus allopurinol.
FAST (Mackenzie et al., Lancet 2020) – non-inferior to allopurinol for CV outcomes.
Gout attacks may increase in the first months – keep taking it
Report chest pain, breathlessness, weakness on one side
Store below 30°C in a dry place, protected from light and moisture. Keep out of the reach of children. Do not use after the expiry date.
